I develop and share public datasets to strengthen the empirical foundations of social science and expand access to knowledge for the public good. ::: {.reversed-list} 1. [**MapAgora, Civic Opportunity Datasets for the Study of American Local Politics and Public Policy**](https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/IRCA7C) [**\[Dashboard\]**](https://snfagora.github.io/agora_dashboard/?fbclid=IwY2xjawLaOfVleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFjN0hpbTRmazRGM0FYVmdaAR6ipZf2atKm8y3rkaz7pwGfldXbCz7spdjecvdG2-BN0S7EApa2LNc_vJU-qQ_aem_f1h1LN8V-5OmYqn207OZsw) [**\[Website\]**](https://snfagora.github.io/modern_agora_dashboard/#about) - **Summary:** We introduce MapAgora, a set of five new datasets that provide a comprehensive view of civic opportunity across America. Drawing on IRS tax records and the websites of over 1.7 million nonprofit organizations, we examine whether organizations offer civic opportunities, such as membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action, and classify them by type (e.g., political, professional, issue-based). The de-identified organization-level dataset includes indicators of civic opportunity, organizational type, and financial status. Four additional datasets aggregate this information at the ZIP code and county levels. We validate that civic opportunity is conceptually distinct from financial resources at the organizational level, while aggregate patterns align with traditional measures of socioeconomic inequality. These datasets offer new tools for understanding civic infrastructure, local democracy, and public policy.\ - **Use case:** Featured in [*"MapAgora, Civic Opportunity Datasets for the Study of American Local Politics and Public Policy"*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-025-05353-6), *Nature: Scientific Data* (2025), and [*"The Unequal Landscape of Civic Opportunity in America"*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-023-01743-1), *Nature Human Behaviour* (2023), with Milan de Vries and Hahrie Han\ - **Collaborator:** Milan de Vries and Hahrie Han 1. [**Validated Names for Experimental Studies on Ethnicity and Race**](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/LP4EAR) [**\[Dashboard\]**](https://jaeyk.github.io/select_validated_names/?fbclid=IwY2xjawP0TOlleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFIdVoxek4zU0p0SFhzZXZJc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHm5a4tquUfrPydahJ1v3TX_HaLK7plqgT8aORGfWqVaYnyGDFhm4VdK0zE_h_aem_KusnJygN3w44M1hksHeycw) - **Summary:** A large and fast-growing number of studies across the social sciences use names in experiments to signal race. However, names may also convey other perceived attributes such as socioeconomic status and citizenship. This dataset provides the largest collection of validated name perceptions to date, based on three U.S. surveys. It includes 44,170 evaluations from 4,026 respondents for 600 names, with ratings of perceived race, income, education, and citizenship, along with respondent characteristics. These data are designed to help researchers isolate the causal effects of race in experimental research.\ - **Use case:** Featured in [*"Validated names for experimental studies on race and ethnicity"*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-023-01947-0), *Nature: Scientific Data* (2023), with Charles Crabtree, S. Michael Gaddis, John B. Holbein, Cameron Guage, and William Marx.\ - **Collaborator:** Charles Crabtree, S. Michael Gaddis, John B. Holbein, Cameron Guage, and William Marx 1. [**Asian American and Latino Advocacy and Community Service Organizations Dataset**](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/FLUPBJ) [**\[Dashboard\]**](https://jaeyk.github.io/aa_latino_organizations_map/) - **Summary:** A historical dataset documenting over 800 nonprofit organizations serving Asian American and Latino communities in the U.S. from 1868 to 2016. It includes founding years, organizational types (advocacy, service, hybrid), and panethnic status. The dataset captures both early ethnic organizations and those that evolved into panethnic entities, such as the National Council of La Raza (NCLR). Validation relied on websites, news archives, and outreach, with founding dates confirmed for 77% of Asian and 71% of Latino organizations.\ - **Use case:** Used in [*"How Other Minorities Gained Access: The War on Poverty and Asian American and Latino Community Organizing"*](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1065912920983456), *Political Research Quarterly* (2021). :::

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  var searchInput = document.querySelector('#quarto-search input[type="text"], .aa-Input');
  if (searchInput) {
    searchInput.setAttribute('placeholder', 'Search this site...');
  }

  // Auto-size reversed list numbering from actual item count.
  document.querySelectorAll('.reversed-list > ol').forEach(function(ol) {
    var wrapper = ol.closest('.reversed-list');
    if (!wrapper) return;

    // Allow manual override via --reversed-counter-reset when needed.
    var manualReset = wrapper.style.getPropertyValue('--reversed-counter-reset');
    if (manualReset && manualReset.trim() !== '') return;

    var itemCount = Array.from(ol.children).filter(function(child) {
      return child.tagName === 'LI';
    }).length;

    wrapper.style.setProperty('--reversed-counter-reset', String(itemCount + 1));
  });
});
</script>
